question_text: Read the following text and fill in each gap with a
stimulus: suitable word based on the information of the text.15 = 5 Eid is the main religious festival of the Muslims in Bangladesh. Eid means happiness. Everyone wants to share this happiness with their near and dear ones. So most of the people, who are living outside their home for different reasons, have a strong desire to get back home during the Eid vacation. As a result, there is a mad rush in the buses, trains and launches for the home-bound people. These often cause transport accidents that take away many lives. However, it cannot stop people's desire to meet their family, in-law or friends. What makes people rush for their homes in spite of serious hazards? This is the pull of the roots. It's these roots that make a bond between us and family members. in-laws, friends, neighbours or even Board & Test Questions : First Paper between us and the land where we were born and grew up. In that sense our families, land of birth, relatives, our culture, tradition or surroundings are our roots. And wherever we stay, we have a continuous pull of our roots. It's our root that develop our identity making us what we are. When we lose the bond, we become rootless. Human beings, who do not have any root or contexts are non entity. In other world they do not have their own identity. Such persons are devoid of values, humanity and social responsibilities. They don't know where they are from, and/or where they are heading towards. This often makes them feel empty and lost. [Unit-12; Lesson-1] In Bangladesh, Eid is the greatest (a) ⎯ of the Muslims. It is celebrated by (b) ⎯ happiness with their near and dear ones. So during Eid vacations, people (c) ⎯ outside their homes try to get back their homes very strongly. This is called a pull of the roots. Roots are the (d) ⎯ of us. The (e) ⎯ persons are devoid of values, humanity and social responsibilities. Read the passage and answer the questions 4 and 5. Louise Pasteur was a French chemist and microbiologist. He is remembered for his remarkable invention of the causes and preventions of diseases. He was born on December 27, 1822 in Dole, Jura, France. He entered primary school in 1831. In 1838 he left for Paris to join the institute of Barbet but became homesick and returned home. In 1839 he got into the college Royal de Beasancon and received B.A. degree in 1840. He did his B.Sc. in Chemistry from Dijon in 1842. He received his medical licence in 1845 as a doctor. He was appointed Professor of Physics at the Dijon Lycee in 1848. He invented the vaccines for Rabies in 1886. He died on September 28, 1895 at the age of 72.
